title: AKS Deployments, Services, and Ingress
description: Deploy applications to AKS using Deployments and Services, and configure Ingress for external HTTP access.

data.text: Deploying an application to AKS involves creating Kubernetes resources using YAML manifests. The primary resource for running containers is the Deployment, and the Service resource exposes it to network traffic.

A Kubernetes Service provides a stable network endpoint for Pods. Since Pods are ephemeral and can be recreated, Services ensure that other components can always reach your application via a consistent address.

data.title: YAML - ClusterIP Service
data.content:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: myapp-service
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  selector:
    app: myapp
  ports:
  - port: 80
    targetPort: 8080
    protocol: TCP

data.text: An Ingress resource manages external HTTP/HTTPS access to Services inside the cluster. On AKS, you typically install an Ingress controller like NGINX Ingress or Azure Application Gateway Ingress Controller to handle the actual routing.

data.title: YAML - Ingress Resource
data.content:
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: myapp-ingress
  annotations:
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/rewrite-target: /
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx
  rules:
  - host: myapp.eastus.cloudapp.azure.com
    http:
      paths:
      - path: /
        pathType: Prefix
        backend:
          service:
            name: myapp-service
            port:
              number: 80

data.title: Azure Application Gateway Ingress Controller
data.text: For production AKS deployments, use the Azure Application Gateway Ingress Controller (AGIC) for WAF protection, SSL termination, and integration with Azure networking.

data.title: Azure CLI - Get AKS Credentials
data.content:
# Connect kubectl to your AKS cluster
az aks get-credentials --resource-group myRG --name myAKS

# Verify connection
kubectl get nodes

# Apply a deployment
kubectl apply -f deployment.yaml

# View running pods
kubectl get pods

# View service endpoints
kubectl get services

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Deployments manage Pod replicas and updates
Services provide stable network access to Pods
Ingress routes external HTTP traffic to Services
Use AGIC for production-grade ingress with WAF
data.takeaway: Deployments, Services, and Ingress are the core Kubernetes primitives for exposing applications.
